title: Where DB code lives (runtimes)
summary: APIs, Next.js server routes, and SPAs — credentials never ship to the browser.

example.code: -- Postgres only reachable from compose network / server
example.sql: -- Postgres only reachable from compose network / server

exercise.prompt: Answer every question — each wrong option explains why it is wrong.

questions.prompt: A React SPA (Vite) shows a list of magazines. Where does the ORM / SQL query run?

options.text: Inside the React component, in useEffect
options.why: That code runs in the browser: DATABASE_URL would ship in the JS bundle, and browsers cannot open a Postgres connection anyway.

options.text: In an API (Node/Express, FastAPI, a Next.js route handler) that the SPA calls over HTTP

options.why: A service worker is still the user's browser — same credential leak, no TCP to Postgres.

questions.prompt: Next.js App Router: which file may import PrismaClient / a DB pool?

options.why: 'use client' components are bundled for the browser; Next.js refuses server-only modules there.

options.text: A Server Component or app/api/…/route.ts route handler

options.why: That is build configuration, not request-time code — it never serves data.

questions.prompt: Where should the database URL live in a Next.js app?

options.why: NEXT_PUBLIC_* variables are inlined into the client bundle — anyone can read the password.

options.text: DATABASE_URL, read only in server code

options.why: It ends up in git history and in any bundle that imports the file.

questions.prompt: Plain Node vs React vs Next: which one is a runtime, which a UI library, which a framework?

options.text: Node = JS runtime (servers, scripts); React = UI library; Next.js = React framework with a server
All three are interchangeable web frameworks
options.why: Node runs JavaScript outside the browser, React only renders UI, Next.js combines React with server rendering and routes.

options.text: React can talk to Postgres directly because it is JavaScript
options.why: React code runs where it is rendered; in the browser it has no DB access and must call an API.

body:
APIs, Next.js server routes, and SPAs — credentials never ship to the browser.

Why it matters: Putting DATABASE_URL in client JS leaks secrets. Production hubs keep runners and queries on the server (this app's /api BFF is the learner-facing example).

SQL ↔ ORM: Browser → https://localhost:3000/api/* → internal runners → Postgres.
why: Putting DATABASE_URL in client JS leaks secrets. Production hubs keep runners and queries on the server (this app's /api BFF is the learner-facing example).
objectives: List safe places for DB access (API process, Next route handlers, workers).
Explain why SPAs must call an API instead of opening Postgres.
pitfalls: Edge runtimes without native driver support — prefer Node for DB labs.
teachAlong: Cause: learner picks a track in the UI.
Effect: BFF routes to python or node runner internally.
You never start a separate 'Python stack' or 'Node stack'.
